GV.name: GOVERN
GV.text: The organization's cybersecurity risk management strategy, expectations, and policy are established, communicated, and monitored

ID.name: IDENTIFY
ID.text: The organization's current cybersecurity risks are understood

PR.name: PROTECT
PR.text: Safeguards to manage the organization's cybersecurity risks are used

DE.name: DETECT
DE.text: Possible cybersecurity attacks and compromises are found and analyzed

RS.name: RESPOND
RS.text: Actions regarding a detected cybersecurity incident are taken

RC.name: RECOVER
RC.text: Assets and operations affected by a cybersecurity incident are restored

GV.OV.title: Oversight
GV.OV.text: Results of organization-wide cybersecurity risk management activities and performance are used to inform, improve, and adjust the risk management strategy

ID.AM.title: Asset Management
ID.AM.text: Assets (e.g., data, hardware, software, systems, facilities, services, people) that enable the organization to achieve business purposes are identified and managed consistent with their relative importance to organizational objectives and the organization's risk strategy

ID.RA.title: Risk Assessment
ID.RA.text: The cybersecurity risk to the organization, assets, and individuals is understood by the organization

PR.AA.title: Identity Management, Authentication, and Access Control

PR.AT.title: Awareness and Training
PR.AT.text: The organization's personnel are provided with cybersecurity awareness and training so that they can perform their cybersecurity-related tasks

PR.DS.title: Data Security
PR.DS.text: Data are managed consistent with the organization's risk strategy to protect the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of information

PR.PS.title: Platform Security
PR.PS.text: The hardware, software (e.g., firmware, operating systems, applications), and services of physical and virtual platforms are managed consistent with the organization's risk strategy to protect their confidentiality, integrity, and availability

PR.IR.title: Technology Infrastructure Resilience
PR.IR.text: Security architectures are managed with the organization's risk strategy to protect asset confidentiality, integrity, and availability, and organizational resilience

PR.AC.title: Identity Management, Authentication and Access Control

DE.CM.title: Continuous Monitoring
DE.CM.text: Assets are monitored to find anomalies, indicators of compromise, and other potentially adverse events

RS.MA.title: Incident Management
RS.MA.text: Responses to detected cybersecurity incidents are managed

RS.AN.title: Incident Analysis
RS.AN.text: Investigations are conducted to ensure effective response and support forensics and recovery activities

RS.CO.title: Incident Response Reporting and Communication
RS.CO.text: Response activities are coordinated with internal and external stakeholders as required by laws, regulations, or policies

RS.MI.title: Incident Mitigation
RS.MI.text: Activities are performed to prevent expansion of an event and mitigate its effects

RC.RP.title: Incident Recovery Plan Execution
RC.RP.text: Restoration activities are performed to ensure operational availability of systems and services affected by cybersecurity incidents

RC.CO.title: Incident Recovery Communication
RC.CO.text: Restoration activities are coordinated with internal and external parties

subcategories.text: The organizational mission is understood and informs cybersecurity risk management

implementation_examples.title: Ex1
implementation_examples.text: Share the organization's mission (e.g., through vision and mission statements, marketing, and service strategies) to provide a basis for identifying risks that may impede that mission

subcategories.text: Internal and external stakeholders are understood, and their needs and expectations regarding cybersecurity risk management are understood and considered

implementation_examples.title: Ex1
implementation_examples.text: Identify relevant internal stakeholders and their cybersecurity-related expectations (e.g., performance and risk expectations of officers, directors, and advisors; cultural expectations of employees)

implementation_examples.title: Ex2
implementation_examples.text: Identify relevant external stakeholders and their cybersecurity-related expectations (e.g., privacy expectations of customers, business expectations of partnerships, compliance expectations of regulators, ethics expectations of society)

subcategories.text: Legal, regulatory, and contractual requirements regarding cybersecurity - including privacy and civil liberties obligations - are understood and managed

implementation_examples.title: Ex1
implementation_examples.text: Determine a process to track and manage legal and regulatory requirements regarding protection of individuals' information (e.g., Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act, California Consumer Privacy Act, General Data Protection Regulation)

implementation_examples.title: Ex2
implementation_examples.text: Determine a process to track and manage contractual requirements for cybersecurity management of supplier, customer, and partner information

implementation_examples.title: Ex3
implementation_examples.text: Align the organization's cybersecurity strategy with legal, regulatory, and contractual requirements

subcategories.text: Critical objectives, capabilities, and services that external stakeholders depend on or expect from the organization are understood and communicated

implementation_examples.title: Ex1
implementation_examples.text: Establish criteria for determining the criticality of capabilities and services as viewed by internal and external stakeholders

implementation_examples.title: Ex2
implementation_examples.text: Determine (e.g., from a business impact analysis) assets and business operations that are vital to achieving mission objectives and the potential impact of a loss (or partial loss) of such operations

implementation_examples.title: Ex3
implementation_examples.text: Establish and communicate resilience objectives (e.g., recovery time objectives) for delivering critical capabilities and services in various operating states (e.g., under attack, during recovery, normal operation)

subcategories.text: Outcomes, capabilities, and services that the organization depends on are understood and communicated

implementation_examples.title: Ex1
implementation_examples.text: Create an inventory of the organization's dependencies on external resources (e.g., facilities, cloud-based hosting providers) and their relationships to organizational assets and business functions

implementation_examples.title: Ex2
implementation_examples.text: Identify and document external dependencies that are potential points of failure for the organization's critical capabilities and services, and share that information with appropriate personnel

subcategories.text: Risk management objectives are established and agreed to by organizational stakeholders

implementation_examples.title: Ex1
implementation_examples.text: Update near-term and long-term cybersecurity risk management objectives as part of annual strategic planning and when major changes occur

implementation_examples.title: Ex2
implementation_examples.text: Establish measurable objectives for cybersecurity risk management (e.g., manage the quality of user training, ensure adequate risk protection for industrial control systems)

implementation_examples.title: Ex3
implementation_examples.text: Senior leaders agree about cybersecurity objectives and use them for measuring and managing risk and performance

subcategories.text: Risk appetite and risk tolerance statements are established, communicated, and maintained

implementation_examples.title: Ex1
implementation_examples.text: Determine and communicate risk appetite statements that convey expectations about the appropriate level of risk for the organization

implementation_examples.title: Ex2
implementation_examples.text: Translate risk appetite statements into specific, measurable, and broadly understandable risk tolerance statements

implementation_examples.title: Ex3
implementation_examples.text: Refine organizational objectives and risk appetite periodically based on known risk exposure and residual risk

subcategories.text: Cybersecurity risk management activities and outcomes are included in enterprise risk management processes

implementation_examples.title: Ex1
implementation_examples.text: Aggregate and manage cybersecurity risks alongside other enterprise risks (e.g., compliance, financial, operational, regulatory, reputational, safety)

implementation_examples.title: Ex2
implementation_examples.text: Include cybersecurity risk managers in enterprise risk management planning

implementation_examples.title: Ex3
implementation_examples.text: Establish criteria for escalating cybersecurity risks within enterprise risk management

subcategories.text: Strategic direction that describes appropriate risk response options is established and communicated

implementation_examples.title: Ex1
implementation_examples.text: Specify criteria for accepting and avoiding cybersecurity risk for various classifications of data

implementation_examples.title: Ex2
implementation_examples.text: Determine whether to purchase cybersecurity insurance

implementation_examples.title: Ex3
implementation_examples.text: Document conditions under which shared responsibility models are acceptable (e.g., outsourcing certain cybersecurity functions, having a third party perform financial transactions on behalf of the organization, using public cloud-based services)

subcategories.text: Lines of communication across the organization are established for cybersecurity risks, including risks from suppliers and other third parties

implementation_examples.title: Ex1
implementation_examples.text: Determine how to update senior executives, directors, and management on the organization's cybersecurity posture at agreed-upon intervals

implementation_examples.title: Ex2
implementation_examples.text: Identify how all departments across the organization - such as management, operations, internal auditors, legal, acquisition, physical security, and HR - will communicate with each other about cybersecurity risks

subcategories.text: A standardized method for calculating, documenting, categorizing, and prioritizing cybersecurity risks is established and communicated

implementation_examples.title: Ex1
implementation_examples.text: Establish criteria for using a quantitative approach to cybersecurity risk analysis, and specify probability and exposure formulas

implementation_examples.title: Ex2
implementation_examples.text: Create and use templates (e.g., a risk register) to document cybersecurity risk information (e.g., risk description, exposure, treatment, and ownership)

implementation_examples.title: Ex3
implementation_examples.text: Establish criteria for risk prioritization at the appropriate levels within the enterprise

implementation_examples.title: Ex4
implementation_examples.text: Use a consistent list of risk categories to support integrating, aggregating, and comparing cybersecurity risks

subcategories.text: Strategic opportunities (i.e., positive risks) are characterized and are included in organizational cybersecurity risk discussions

implementation_examples.title: Ex1
implementation_examples.text: Define and communicate guidance and methods for identifying opportunities and including them in risk discussions (e.g., strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, and threats [SWOT] analysis)

implementation_examples.title: Ex2
implementation_examples.text: Identify stretch goals and document them

implementation_examples.title: Ex3
implementation_examples.text: Calculate, document, and prioritize positive risks alongside negative risks

subcategories.text: Organizational leadership is responsible and accountable for cybersecurity risk and fosters a culture that is risk-aware, ethical, and continually improving

implementation_examples.title: Ex1
implementation_examples.text: Leaders (e.g., directors) agree on their roles and responsibilities in developing, implementing, and assessing the organization's cybersecurity strategy

implementation_examples.title: Ex2
implementation_examples.text: Share leaders' expectations regarding a secure and ethical culture, especially when current events present the opportunity to highlight positive or negative examples of cybersecurity risk management

implementation_examples.title: Ex3
implementation_examples.text: Leaders direct the CISO to maintain a comprehensive cybersecurity risk strategy and review and update it at least annually and after major events

implementation_examples.title: Ex4
implementation_examples.text: Conduct reviews to ensure adequate authority and coordination among those responsible for managing cybersecurity risk

subcategories.text: Roles, responsibilities, and authorities related to cybersecurity risk management are established, communicated, understood, and enforced

implementation_examples.title: Ex1
implementation_examples.text: Document risk management roles and responsibilities in policy

implementation_examples.title: Ex2
implementation_examples.text: Document who is responsible and accountable for cybersecurity risk management activities and how those teams and individuals are to be consulted and informed

implementation_examples.title: Ex3
implementation_examples.text: Include cybersecurity responsibilities and performance requirements in personnel descriptions

implementation_examples.title: Ex4
implementation_examples.text: Document performance goals for personnel with cybersecurity risk management responsibilities, and periodically measure performance to identify areas for improvement

implementation_examples.title: Ex5
implementation_examples.text: Clearly articulate cybersecurity responsibilities within operations, risk functions, and internal audit functions

subcategories.text: Adequate resources are allocated commensurate with the cybersecurity risk strategy, roles, responsibilities, and policies

implementation_examples.title: Ex1
implementation_examples.text: Conduct periodic management reviews to ensure that those given cybersecurity risk management responsibilities have the necessary authority

implementation_examples.title: Ex2
implementation_examples.text: Identify resource allocation and investment in line with risk tolerance and response

implementation_examples.title: Ex3
implementation_examples.text: Provide adequate and sufficient people, process, and technical resources to support the cybersecurity strategy

subcategories.text: Cybersecurity is included in human resources practices

implementation_examples.title: Ex1
implementation_examples.text: Integrate cybersecurity risk management considerations into human resources processes (e.g., personnel screening, onboarding, change notification, offboarding)

implementation_examples.title: Ex2
implementation_examples.text: Consider cybersecurity knowledge to be a positive factor in hiring, training, and retention decisions

implementation_examples.title: Ex3
implementation_examples.text: Conduct background checks prior to onboarding new personnel for sensitive roles, and periodically repeat background checks for personnel with such roles

implementation_examples.title: Ex4
implementation_examples.text: Define and enforce obligations for personnel to be aware of, adhere to, and uphold security policies as they relate to their roles

subcategories.text: Policy for managing cybersecurity risks is established based on organizational context, cybersecurity strategy, and priorities and is communicated and enforced

implementation_examples.title: Ex1
implementation_examples.text: Create, disseminate, and maintain an understandable, usable risk management policy with statements of management intent, expectations, and direction

implementation_examples.title: Ex2
implementation_examples.text: Periodically review policy and supporting processes and procedures to ensure that they align with risk management strategy objectives and priorities, as well as the high-level direction of the cybersecurity policy

implementation_examples.title: Ex3
implementation_examples.text: Require approval from senior management on policy

implementation_examples.title: Ex4
implementation_examples.text: Communicate cybersecurity risk management policy and supporting processes and procedures across the organization

implementation_examples.title: Ex5
implementation_examples.text: Require personnel to acknowledge receipt of policy when first hired, annually, and whenever policy is updated

subcategories.text: Policy for managing cybersecurity risks is reviewed, updated, communicated, and enforced to reflect changes in requirements, threats, technology, and organizational mission

implementation_examples.title: Ex1
implementation_examples.text: Update policy based on periodic reviews of cybersecurity risk management results to ensure that policy and supporting processes and procedures adequately maintain risk at an acceptable level

implementation_examples.title: Ex2
implementation_examples.text: Provide a timeline for reviewing changes to the organization's risk environment (e.g., changes in risk or in the organization's mission objectives), and communicate recommended policy updates

implementation_examples.title: Ex3
implementation_examples.text: Update policy to reflect changes in legal and regulatory requirements

implementation_examples.title: Ex4
implementation_examples.text: Update policy to reflect changes in technology (e.g., adoption of artificial intelligence) and changes to the business (e.g., acquisition of a new business, new contract requirements)

subcategories.category_text: Results of organization-wide cybersecurity risk management activities and performance are used to inform, improve, and adjust the risk management strategy
subcategories.text: Cybersecurity risk management strategy outcomes are reviewed to inform and adjust strategy and direction

implementation_examples.title: Ex1
implementation_examples.text: Measure how well the risk management strategy and risk results have helped leaders make decisions and achieve organizational objectives

implementation_examples.title: Ex2
implementation_examples.text: Examine whether cybersecurity risk strategies that impede operations or innovation should be adjusted

subcategories.category_text: Results of organization-wide cybersecurity risk management activities and performance are used to inform, improve, and adjust the risk management strategy
subcategories.text: The cybersecurity risk management strategy is reviewed and adjusted to ensure coverage of organizational requirements and risks

implementation_examples.title: Ex1
implementation_examples.text: Review audit findings to confirm whether the existing cybersecurity strategy has ensured compliance with internal and external requirements

implementation_examples.title: Ex2
implementation_examples.text: Review the performance oversight of those in cybersecurity-related roles to determine whether policy changes are necessary

implementation_examples.title: Ex3
implementation_examples.text: Review strategy in light of cybersecurity incidents

subcategories.category_text: Results of organization-wide cybersecurity risk management activities and performance are used to inform, improve, and adjust the risk management strategy
subcategories.text: Organizational cybersecurity risk management performance is evaluated and reviewed for adjustments needed

implementation_examples.title: Ex1
implementation_examples.text: Review key performance indicators (KPIs) to ensure that organization-wide policies and procedures achieve objectives

implementation_examples.title: Ex2
implementation_examples.text: Review key risk indicators (KRIs) to identify risks the organization faces, including likelihood and potential impact

implementation_examples.title: Ex3
implementation_examples.text: Collect and communicate metrics on cybersecurity risk management with senior leadership

subcategories.text: A cybersecurity supply chain risk management program, strategy, objectives, policies, and processes are established and agreed to by organizational stakeholders

implementation_examples.title: Ex1
implementation_examples.text: Establish a strategy that expresses the objectives of the cybersecurity supply chain risk management program

implementation_examples.title: Ex2
implementation_examples.text: Develop the cybersecurity supply chain risk management program, including a plan (with milestones), policies, and procedures that guide implementation and improvement of the program, and share the policies and procedures with the organizational stakeholders

implementation_examples.title: Ex3
implementation_examples.text: Develop and implement program processes based on the strategy, objectives, policies, and procedures that are agreed upon and performed by the organizational stakeholders

implementation_examples.title: Ex4
implementation_examples.text: Establish a cross-organizational mechanism that ensures alignment between functions that contribute to cybersecurity supply chain risk management, such as cybersecurity, IT, operations, legal, human resources, and engineering

subcategories.text: Cybersecurity roles and responsibilities for suppliers, customers, and partners are established, communicated, and coordinated internally and externally

implementation_examples.title: Ex1
implementation_examples.text: Identify one or more specific roles or positions that will be responsible and accountable for planning, resourcing, and executing cybersecurity supply chain risk management activities

implementation_examples.title: Ex2
implementation_examples.text: Document cybersecurity supply chain risk management roles and responsibilities in policy

implementation_examples.title: Ex3
implementation_examples.text: Create responsibility matrixes to document who will be responsible and accountable for cybersecurity supply chain risk management activities and how those teams and individuals will be consulted and informed

implementation_examples.title: Ex4
implementation_examples.text: Include cybersecurity supply chain risk management responsibilities and performance requirements in personnel descriptions to ensure clarity and improve accountability

implementation_examples.title: Ex5
implementation_examples.text: Document performance goals for personnel with cybersecurity risk management-specific responsibilities, and periodically measure them to demonstrate and improve performance

implementation_examples.title: Ex6
implementation_examples.text: Develop roles and responsibilities for suppliers, customers, and business partners to address shared responsibilities for applicable cybersecurity risks, and integrate them into organizational policies and applicable third-party agreements

implementation_examples.title: Ex7
implementation_examples.text: Internally communicate cybersecurity supply chain risk management roles and responsibilities for third parties

implementation_examples.title: Ex8
implementation_examples.text: Establish rules and protocols for information sharing and reporting processes between the organization and its suppliers

subcategories.text: Cybersecurity supply chain risk management is integrated into cybersecurity and enterprise risk management, risk assessment, and improvement processes

implementation_examples.title: Ex1
implementation_examples.text: Identify areas of alignment and overlap with cybersecurity and enterprise risk management

implementation_examples.title: Ex2
implementation_examples.text: Establish integrated control sets for cybersecurity risk management and cybersecurity supply chain risk management

implementation_examples.title: Ex3
implementation_examples.text: Integrate cybersecurity supply chain risk management into improvement processes

implementation_examples.title: Ex4
implementation_examples.text: Escalate material cybersecurity risks in supply chains to senior management, and address them at the enterprise risk management level

subcategories.text: Suppliers are known and prioritized by criticality

implementation_examples.title: Ex1
implementation_examples.text: Develop criteria for supplier criticality based on, for example, the sensitivity of data processed or possessed by suppliers, the degree of access to the organization's systems, and the importance of the products or services to the organization's mission

implementation_examples.title: Ex2
implementation_examples.text: Keep a record of all suppliers, and prioritize suppliers based on the criticality criteria

subcategories.text: Requirements to address cybersecurity risks in supply chains are established, prioritized, and integrated into contracts and other types of agreements with suppliers and other relevant third parties

implementation_examples.title: Ex1
implementation_examples.text: Establish security requirements for suppliers, products, and services commensurate with their criticality level and potential impact if compromised

implementation_examples.title: Ex2
implementation_examples.text: Include all cybersecurity and supply chain requirements that third parties must follow and how compliance with the requirements may be verified in default contractual language

implementation_examples.title: Ex3
implementation_examples.text: Define the rules and protocols for information sharing between the organization and its suppliers and sub-tier suppliers in agreements

implementation_examples.title: Ex4
implementation_examples.text: Manage risk by including security requirements in agreements based on their criticality and potential impact if compromised

implementation_examples.title: Ex5
implementation_examples.text: Define security requirements in service-level agreements (SLAs) for monitoring suppliers for acceptable security performance throughout the supplier relationship lifecycle

implementation_examples.title: Ex6
implementation_examples.text: Contractually require suppliers to disclose cybersecurity features, functions, and vulnerabilities of their products and services for the life of the product or the term of service

implementation_examples.title: Ex7
implementation_examples.text: Contractually require suppliers to provide and maintain a current component inventory (e.g., software or hardware bill of materials) for critical products

implementation_examples.title: Ex8
implementation_examples.text: Contractually require suppliers to vet their employees and guard against insider threats

implementation_examples.title: Ex9
implementation_examples.text: Contractually require suppliers to provide evidence of performing acceptable security practices through, for example, self-attestation, conformance to known standards, certifications, or inspections

implementation_examples.title: Ex10
implementation_examples.text: Specify in contracts and other agreements the rights and responsibilities of the organization, its suppliers, and their supply chains, with respect to potential cybersecurity risks

subcategories.text: Planning and due diligence are performed to reduce risks before entering into formal supplier or other third-party relationships

implementation_examples.title: Ex1
implementation_examples.text: Perform thorough due diligence on prospective suppliers that is consistent with procurement planning and commensurate with the level of risk, criticality, and complexity of each supplier relationship

implementation_examples.title: Ex2
implementation_examples.text: Assess the suitability of the technology and cybersecurity capabilities and the risk management practices of prospective suppliers

implementation_examples.title: Ex3
implementation_examples.text: Conduct supplier risk assessments against business and applicable cybersecurity requirements

implementation_examples.title: Ex4
implementation_examples.text: Assess the authenticity, integrity, and security of critical products prior to acquisition and use

subcategories.text: The risks posed by a supplier, their products and services, and other third parties are understood, recorded, prioritized, assessed, responded to, and monitored over the course of the relationship

implementation_examples.title: Ex1
implementation_examples.text: Adjust assessment formats and frequencies based on the third party's reputation and the criticality of the products or services they provide

implementation_examples.title: Ex2
implementation_examples.text: Evaluate third parties' evidence of compliance with contractual cybersecurity requirements, such as self-attestations, warranties, certifications, and other artifacts

implementation_examples.title: Ex3
implementation_examples.text: Monitor critical suppliers to ensure that they are fulfilling their security obligations throughout the supplier relationship lifecycle using a variety of methods and techniques, such as inspections, audits, tests, or other forms of evaluation

implementation_examples.title: Ex4
implementation_examples.text: Monitor critical suppliers, services, and products for changes to their risk profiles, and reevaluate supplier criticality and risk impact accordingly

implementation_examples.title: Ex5
implementation_examples.text: Plan for unexpected supplier and supply chain-related interruptions to ensure business continuity

subcategories.text: Relevant suppliers and other third parties are included in incident planning, response, and recovery activities

implementation_examples.title: Ex1
implementation_examples.text: Define and use rules and protocols for reporting incident response and recovery activities and the status between the organization and its suppliers

implementation_examples.title: Ex2
implementation_examples.text: Identify and document the roles and responsibilities of the organization and its suppliers for incident response

implementation_examples.title: Ex3
implementation_examples.text: Include critical suppliers in incident response exercises and simulations

implementation_examples.title: Ex4
implementation_examples.text: Define and coordinate crisis communication methods and protocols between the organization and its critical suppliers

implementation_examples.title: Ex5
implementation_examples.text: Conduct collaborative lessons learned sessions with critical suppliers

subcategories.text: Supply chain security practices are integrated into cybersecurity and enterprise risk management programs, and their performance is monitored throughout the technology product and service life cycle

implementation_examples.title: Ex1
implementation_examples.text: Policies and procedures require provenance records for all acquired technology products and services

implementation_examples.title: Ex2
implementation_examples.text: Periodically provide risk reporting to leaders about how acquired components are proven to be untampered and authentic

implementation_examples.title: Ex3
implementation_examples.text: Communicate regularly among cybersecurity risk managers and operations personnel about the need to acquire software patches, updates, and upgrades only from authenticated and trustworthy software providers

implementation_examples.title: Ex4
implementation_examples.text: Review policies to ensure that they require approved supplier personnel to perform maintenance on supplier products

implementation_examples.title: Ex5
implementation_examples.text: Policies and procedure require checking upgrades to critical hardware for unauthorized changes

subcategories.text: Cybersecurity supply chain risk management plans include provisions for activities that occur after the conclusion of a partnership or service agreement

implementation_examples.title: Ex1
implementation_examples.text: Establish processes for terminating critical relationships under both normal and adverse circumstances

implementation_examples.title: Ex2
implementation_examples.text: Define and implement plans for component end-of-life maintenance support and obsolescence

implementation_examples.title: Ex3
implementation_examples.text: Verify that supplier access to organization resources is deactivated promptly when it is no longer needed

implementation_examples.title: Ex4
implementation_examples.text: Verify that assets containing the organization's data are returned or properly disposed of in a timely, controlled, and safe manner

implementation_examples.title: Ex5
implementation_examples.text: Develop and execute a plan for terminating or transitioning supplier relationships that takes supply chain security risk and resiliency into account

implementation_examples.title: Ex6
implementation_examples.text: Mitigate risks to data and systems created by supplier termination

implementation_examples.title: Ex7
implementation_examples.text: Manage data leakage risks associated with supplier termination

subcategories.category_text: Assets (e.g., data, hardware, software, systems, facilities, services, people) that enable the organization to achieve business purposes are identified and managed consistent with their relative importance to organizational objectives and the organization's risk strategy
subcategories.text: Inventories of hardware managed by the organization are maintained

implementation_examples.title: Ex1
implementation_examples.text: Maintain inventories for all types of hardware, including IT, IoT, OT, and mobile devices

implementation_examples.title: Ex2
implementation_examples.text: Constantly monitor networks to detect new hardware and automatically update inventories

subcategories.category_text: Assets (e.g., data, hardware, software, systems, facilities, services, people) that enable the organization to achieve business purposes are identified and managed consistent with their relative importance to organizational objectives and the organization's risk strategy
subcategories.text: Inventories of software, services, and systems managed by the organization are maintained

implementation_examples.title: Ex1
implementation_examples.text: Maintain inventories for all types of software and services, including commercial-off-the-shelf, open-source, custom applications, API services, and cloud-based applications and services

implementation_examples.title: Ex2
implementation_examples.text: Constantly monitor all platforms, including containers and virtual machines, for software and service inventory changes

implementation_examples.title: Ex3
implementation_examples.text: Maintain an inventory of the organization's systems

subcategories.category_text: Assets (e.g., data, hardware, software, systems, facilities, services, people) that enable the organization to achieve business purposes are identified and managed consistent with their relative importance to organizational objectives and the organization's risk strategy
subcategories.text: Representations of the organization's authorized network communication and internal and external network data flows are maintained

implementation_examples.title: Ex1
implementation_examples.text: Maintain baselines of communication and data flows within the organization's wired and wireless networks

implementation_examples.title: Ex2
implementation_examples.text: Maintain baselines of communication and data flows between the organization and third parties

implementation_examples.title: Ex3
implementation_examples.text: Maintain baselines of communication and data flows for the organization's infrastructure-as-a-service (IaaS) usage

implementation_examples.title: Ex4
implementation_examples.text: Maintain documentation of expected network ports, protocols, and services that are typically used among authorized systems

subcategories.category_text: Assets (e.g., data, hardware, software, systems, facilities, services, people) that enable the organization to achieve business purposes are identified and managed consistent with their relative importance to organizational objectives and the organization's risk strategy
subcategories.text: Inventories of services provided by suppliers are maintained

implementation_examples.title: Ex1
implementation_examples.text: Inventory all external services used by the organization, including third-party infrastructure-as-a-service (IaaS), platform-as-a-service (PaaS), and software-as-a-service (SaaS) offerings; APIs; and other externally hosted application services

implementation_examples.title: Ex2
implementation_examples.text: Update the inventory when a new external service is going to be utilized to ensure adequate cybersecurity risk management monitoring of the organization's use of that service

subcategories.category_text: Assets (e.g., data, hardware, software, systems, facilities, services, people) that enable the organization to achieve business purposes are identified and managed consistent with their relative importance to organizational objectives and the organization's risk strategy
subcategories.text: Assets are prioritized based on classification, criticality, resources, and impact on the mission

implementation_examples.title: Ex1
implementation_examples.text: Define criteria for prioritizing each class of assets

implementation_examples.title: Ex2
implementation_examples.text: Apply the prioritization criteria to assets

implementation_examples.title: Ex3
implementation_examples.text: Track the asset priorities and update them periodically or when significant changes to the organization occur

subcategories.category_text: Assets (e.g., data, hardware, software, systems, facilities, services, people) that enable the organization to achieve business purposes are identified and managed consistent with their relative importance to organizational objectives and the organization's risk strategy
subcategories.text: Inventories of data and corresponding metadata for designated data types are maintained

implementation_examples.title: Ex1
implementation_examples.text: Maintain a list of the designated data types of interest (e.g., personally identifiable information, protected health information, financial account numbers, organization intellectual property, operational technology data)

implementation_examples.title: Ex2
implementation_examples.text: Continuously discover and analyze ad hoc data to identify new instances of designated data types

implementation_examples.title: Ex3
implementation_examples.text: Assign data classifications to designated data types through tags or labels

implementation_examples.title: Ex4
implementation_examples.text: Track the provenance, data owner, and geolocation of each instance of designated data types

subcategories.category_text: Assets (e.g., data, hardware, software, systems, facilities, services, people) that enable the organization to achieve business purposes are identified and managed consistent with their relative importance to organizational objectives and the organization's risk strategy
subcategories.text: Systems, hardware, software, services, and data are managed throughout their life cycles

implementation_examples.title: Ex1
implementation_examples.text: Integrate cybersecurity considerations throughout the life cycles of systems, hardware, software, and services

implementation_examples.title: Ex2
implementation_examples.text: Integrate cybersecurity considerations into product life cycles

implementation_examples.title: Ex3
implementation_examples.text: Identify unofficial uses of technology to meet mission objectives (i.e., shadow IT)

implementation_examples.title: Ex4
implementation_examples.text: Periodically identify redundant systems, hardware, software, and services that unnecessarily increase the organization's attack surface

implementation_examples.title: Ex5
implementation_examples.text: Properly configure and secure systems, hardware, software, and services prior to their deployment in production

implementation_examples.title: Ex6
implementation_examples.text: Update inventories when systems, hardware, software, and services are moved or transferred within the organization

implementation_examples.title: Ex7
implementation_examples.text: Securely destroy stored data based on the organization's data retention policy using the prescribed destruction method, and keep and manage a record of the destructions

implementation_examples.title: Ex8
implementation_examples.text: Securely sanitize data storage when hardware is being retired, decommissioned, reassigned, or sent for repairs or replacement

implementation_examples.title: Ex9
implementation_examples.text: Offer methods for destroying paper, storage media, and other physical forms of data storage

subcategories.category_text: The cybersecurity risk to the organization, assets, and individuals is understood by the organization
subcategories.text: Vulnerabilities in assets are identified, validated, and recorded

implementation_examples.title: Ex1
implementation_examples.text: Use vulnerability management technologies to identify unpatched and misconfigured software

implementation_examples.title: Ex2
implementation_examples.text: Assess network and system architectures for design and implementation weaknesses that affect cybersecurity

implementation_examples.title: Ex3
implementation_examples.text: Review, analyze, or test organization-developed software to identify design, coding, and default configuration vulnerabilities

implementation_examples.title: Ex4
implementation_examples.text: Assess facilities that house critical computing assets for physical vulnerabilities and resilience issues

implementation_examples.title: Ex5
implementation_examples.text: Monitor sources of cyber threat intelligence for information on new vulnerabilities in products and services

implementation_examples.title: Ex6
implementation_examples.text: Review processes and procedures for weaknesses that could be exploited to affect cybersecurity

subcategories.category_text: The cybersecurity risk to the organization, assets, and individuals is understood by the organization
subcategories.text: Cyber threat intelligence is received from information sharing forums and sources

implementation_examples.title: Ex1
implementation_examples.text: Configure cybersecurity tools and technologies with detection or response capabilities to securely ingest cyber threat intelligence feeds

implementation_examples.title: Ex2
implementation_examples.text: Receive and review advisories from reputable third parties on current threat actors and their tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs)

implementation_examples.title: Ex3
implementation_examples.text: Monitor sources of cyber threat intelligence for information on the types of vulnerabilities that emerging technologies may have

subcategories.category_text: The cybersecurity risk to the organization, assets, and individuals is understood by the organization
subcategories.text: Internal and external threats to the organization are identified and recorded

implementation_examples.title: Ex1
implementation_examples.text: Use cyber threat intelligence to maintain awareness of the types of threat actors likely to target the organization and the TTPs they are likely to use

implementation_examples.title: Ex2
implementation_examples.text: Perform threat hunting to look for signs of threat actors within the environment

implementation_examples.title: Ex3
implementation_examples.text: Implement processes for identifying internal threat actors

subcategories.category_text: The cybersecurity risk to the organization, assets, and individuals is understood by the organization
subcategories.text: Potential impacts and likelihoods of threats exploiting vulnerabilities are identified and recorded

implementation_examples.title: Ex1
implementation_examples.text: Business leaders and cybersecurity risk management practitioners work together to estimate the likelihood and impact of risk scenarios and record them in risk registers

implementation_examples.title: Ex2
implementation_examples.text: Enumerate the potential business impacts of unauthorized access to the organization's communications, systems, and data processed in or by those systems

implementation_examples.title: Ex3
implementation_examples.text: Account for the potential impacts of cascading failures for systems of systems

subcategories.category_text: The cybersecurity risk to the organization, assets, and individuals is understood by the organization
subcategories.text: Threats, vulnerabilities, likelihoods, and impacts are used to understand inherent risk and inform risk response prioritization

implementation_examples.title: Ex1
implementation_examples.text: Develop threat models to better understand risks to the data and identify appropriate risk responses

implementation_examples.title: Ex2
implementation_examples.text: Prioritize cybersecurity resource allocations and investments based on estimated likelihoods and impacts

subcategories.category_text: The cybersecurity risk to the organization, assets, and individuals is understood by the organization
subcategories.text: Risk responses are chosen, prioritized, planned, tracked, and communicated

implementation_examples.title: Ex1
implementation_examples.text: Apply the vulnerability management plan's criteria for deciding whether to accept, transfer, mitigate, or avoid risk

implementation_examples.title: Ex2
implementation_examples.text: Apply the vulnerability management plan's criteria for selecting compensating controls to mitigate risk

implementation_examples.title: Ex3
implementation_examples.text: Track the progress of risk response implementation (e.g., plan of action and milestones [POA&M], risk register, risk detail report)

implementation_examples.title: Ex4
implementation_examples.text: Use risk assessment findings to inform risk response decisions and actions

implementation_examples.title: Ex5
implementation_examples.text: Communicate planned risk responses to affected stakeholders in priority order

subcategories.category_text: The cybersecurity risk to the organization, assets, and individuals is understood by the organization
subcategories.text: Changes and exceptions are managed, assessed for risk impact, recorded, and tracked

implementation_examples.title: Ex1
implementation_examples.text: Implement and follow procedures for the formal documentation, review, testing, and approval of proposed changes and requested exceptions

implementation_examples.title: Ex2
implementation_examples.text: Document the possible risks of making or not making each proposed change, and provide guidance on rolling back changes

implementation_examples.title: Ex3
implementation_examples.text: Document the risks related to each requested exception and the plan for responding to those risks

implementation_examples.title: Ex4
implementation_examples.text: Periodically review risks that were accepted based upon planned future actions or milestones

subcategories.category_text: The cybersecurity risk to the organization, assets, and individuals is understood by the organization
subcategories.text: Processes for receiving, analyzing, and responding to vulnerability disclosures are established

implementation_examples.title: Ex1
implementation_examples.text: Conduct vulnerability information sharing between the organization and its suppliers following the rules and protocols defined in contracts

implementation_examples.title: Ex2
implementation_examples.text: Assign responsibilities and verify the execution of procedures for processing, analyzing the impact of, and responding to cybersecurity threat, vulnerability, or incident disclosures by suppliers, customers, partners, and government cybersecurity organizations

subcategories.category_text: The cybersecurity risk to the organization, assets, and individuals is understood by the organization
subcategories.text: The authenticity and integrity of hardware and software are assessed prior to acquisition and use

implementation_examples.title: Ex1
implementation_examples.text: Assess the authenticity and cybersecurity of critical technology products and services prior to acquisition and use

subcategories.category_text: The cybersecurity risk to the organization, assets, and individuals is understood by the organization
subcategories.text: Critical suppliers are assessed prior to acquisition

implementation_examples.title: Ex1
implementation_examples.text: Conduct supplier risk assessments against business and applicable cybersecurity requirements, including the supply chain

subcategories.text: Improvements are identified from evaluations

implementation_examples.title: Ex1
implementation_examples.text: Perform self-assessments of critical services that take current threats and TTPs into consideration

implementation_examples.title: Ex2
implementation_examples.text: Invest in third-party assessments or independent audits of the effectiveness of the organization's cybersecurity program to identify areas that need improvement

implementation_examples.title: Ex3
implementation_examples.text: Constantly evaluate compliance with selected cybersecurity requirements through automated means

subcategories.text: Improvements are identified from security tests and exercises, including those done in coordination with suppliers and relevant third parties

implementation_examples.title: Ex1
implementation_examples.text: Identify improvements for future incident response activities based on findings from incident response assessments (e.g., tabletop exercises and simulations, tests, internal reviews, independent audits)

implementation_examples.title: Ex2
implementation_examples.text: Identify improvements for future business continuity, disaster recovery, and incident response activities based on exercises performed in coordination with critical service providers and product suppliers

implementation_examples.title: Ex3
implementation_examples.text: Involve internal stakeholders (e.g., senior executives, legal department, HR) in security tests and exercises as appropriate

implementation_examples.title: Ex4
implementation_examples.text: Perform penetration testing to identify opportunities to improve the security posture of selected high-risk systems as approved by leadership

implementation_examples.title: Ex5
implementation_examples.text: Exercise contingency plans for responding to and recovering from the discovery that products or services did not originate with the contracted supplier or partner or were altered before receipt

implementation_examples.title: Ex6
implementation_examples.text: Collect and analyze performance metrics using security tools and services to inform improvements to the cybersecurity program

subcategories.text: Improvements are identified from execution of operational processes, procedures, and activities

implementation_examples.title: Ex1
implementation_examples.text: Conduct collaborative lessons learned sessions with suppliers

implementation_examples.title: Ex2
implementation_examples.text: Annually review cybersecurity policies, processes, and procedures to take lessons learned into account

implementation_examples.title: Ex3
implementation_examples.text: Use metrics to assess operational cybersecurity performance over time

subcategories.text: Incident response plans and other cybersecurity plans that affect operations are established, communicated, maintained, and improved

implementation_examples.title: Ex1
implementation_examples.text: Establish contingency plans (e.g., incident response, business continuity, disaster recovery) for responding to and recovering from adverse events that can interfere with operations, expose confidential information, or otherwise endanger the organization's mission and viability

implementation_examples.title: Ex2
implementation_examples.text: Include contact and communication information, processes for handling common scenarios, and criteria for prioritization, escalation, and elevation in all contingency plans

implementation_examples.title: Ex3
implementation_examples.text: Create a vulnerability management plan to identify and assess all types of vulnerabilities and to prioritize, test, and implement risk responses

implementation_examples.title: Ex4
implementation_examples.text: Communicate cybersecurity plans (including updates) to those responsible for carrying them out and to affected parties

implementation_examples.title: Ex5
implementation_examples.text: Review and update all cybersecurity plans annually or when a need for significant improvements is identified

subcategories.category_name: Identity Management, Authentication, and Access Control
subcategories.text: Identities and credentials for authorized users, services, and hardware are managed by the organization

implementation_examples.title: Ex1
implementation_examples.text: Initiate requests for new access or additional access for employees, contractors, and others, and track, review, and fulfill the requests, with permission from system or data owners when needed

implementation_examples.title: Ex2
implementation_examples.text: Issue, manage, and revoke cryptographic certificates and identity tokens, cryptographic keys (i.e., key management), and other credentials

implementation_examples.title: Ex3
implementation_examples.text: Select a unique identifier for each device from immutable hardware characteristics or an identifier securely provisioned to the device

implementation_examples.title: Ex4
implementation_examples.text: Physically label authorized hardware with an identifier for inventory and servicing purposes

subcategories.category_name: Identity Management, Authentication, and Access Control
subcategories.text: Identities are proofed and bound to credentials based on the context of interactions

implementation_examples.title: Ex1
implementation_examples.text: Verify a person's claimed identity at enrollment time using government-issued identity credentials (e.g., passport, visa, driver's license)

implementation_examples.title: Ex2
implementation_examples.text: Issue a different credential for each person (i.e., no credential sharing)

subcategories.category_name: Identity Management, Authentication, and Access Control
subcategories.text: Users, services, and hardware are authenticated

implementation_examples.title: Ex1
implementation_examples.text: Require multifactor authentication

implementation_examples.title: Ex2
implementation_examples.text: Enforce policies for the minimum strength of passwords, PINs, and similar authenticators

implementation_examples.title: Ex3
implementation_examples.text: Periodically reauthenticate users, services, and hardware based on risk (e.g., in zero trust architectures)

implementation_examples.title: Ex4
implementation_examples.text: Ensure that authorized personnel can access accounts essential for protecting safety under emergency conditions

subcategories.category_name: Identity Management, Authentication, and Access Control
subcategories.text: Identity assertions are protected, conveyed, and verified

implementation_examples.title: Ex1
implementation_examples.text: Protect identity assertions that are used to convey authentication and user information through single sign-on systems

implementation_examples.title: Ex2
implementation_examples.text: Protect identity assertions that are used to convey authentication and user information between federated systems

implementation_examples.title: Ex3
implementation_examples.text: Implement standards-based approaches for identity assertions in all contexts, and follow all guidance for the generation (e.g., data models, metadata), protection (e.g., digital signing, encryption), and verification (e.g., signature validation) of identity assertions

subcategories.category_name: Identity Management, Authentication, and Access Control
subcategories.text: Access permissions, entitlements, and authorizations are defined in a policy, managed, enforced, and reviewed, and incorporate the principles of least privilege and separation of duties

implementation_examples.title: Ex1
implementation_examples.text: Review logical and physical access privileges periodically and whenever someone changes roles or leaves the organization, and promptly rescind privileges that are no longer needed

implementation_examples.title: Ex2
implementation_examples.text: Take attributes of the requester and the requested resource into account for authorization decisions (e.g., geolocation, day/time, requester endpoint's cyber health)

implementation_examples.title: Ex3
implementation_examples.text: Restrict access and privileges to the minimum necessary (e.g., zero trust architecture)

implementation_examples.title: Ex4
implementation_examples.text: Periodically review the privileges associated with critical business functions to confirm proper separation of duties

subcategories.category_name: Identity Management, Authentication, and Access Control
subcategories.text: Physical access to assets is managed, monitored, and enforced commensurate with risk

implementation_examples.title: Ex1
implementation_examples.text: Use security guards, security cameras, locked entrances, alarm systems, and other physical controls to monitor facilities and restrict access

implementation_examples.title: Ex2
implementation_examples.text: Employ additional physical security controls for areas that contain high-risk assets

implementation_examples.title: Ex3
implementation_examples.text: Escort guests, vendors, and other third parties within areas that contain business-critical assets

subcategories.category_text: The organization's personnel are provided with cybersecurity awareness and training so that they can perform their cybersecurity-related tasks
subcategories.text: Personnel are provided with awareness and training so that they possess the knowledge and skills to perform general tasks with cybersecurity risks in mind

implementation_examples.title: Ex1
implementation_examples.text: Provide basic cybersecurity awareness and training to employees, contractors, partners, suppliers, and all other users of the organization's non-public resources

implementation_examples.title: Ex2
implementation_examples.text: Train personnel to recognize social engineering attempts and other common attacks, report attacks and suspicious activity, comply with acceptable use policies, and perform basic cyber hygiene tasks (e.g., patching software, choosing passwords, protecting credentials)

implementation_examples.title: Ex3
implementation_examples.text: Explain the consequences of cybersecurity policy violations, both to individual users and the organization as a whole

implementation_examples.title: Ex4
implementation_examples.text: Periodically assess or test users on their understanding of basic cybersecurity practices

implementation_examples.title: Ex5
implementation_examples.text: Require annual refreshers to reinforce existing practices and introduce new practices

subcategories.category_text: The organization's personnel are provided with cybersecurity awareness and training so that they can perform their cybersecurity-related tasks
subcategories.text: Individuals in specialized roles are provided with awareness and training so that they possess the knowledge and skills to perform relevant tasks with cybersecurity risks in mind

implementation_examples.title: Ex1
implementation_examples.text: Identify the specialized roles within the organization that require additional cybersecurity training, such as physical and cybersecurity personnel, finance personnel, senior leadership, and anyone with access to business-critical data

implementation_examples.title: Ex2
implementation_examples.text: Provide role-based cybersecurity awareness and training to all those in specialized roles, including contractors, partners, suppliers, and other third parties

implementation_examples.title: Ex3
implementation_examples.text: Periodically assess or test users on their understanding of cybersecurity practices for their specialized roles

implementation_examples.title: Ex4
implementation_examples.text: Require annual refreshers to reinforce existing practices and introduce new practices

subcategories.category_text: Data are managed consistent with the organization's risk strategy to protect the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of information
subcategories.text: The confidentiality, integrity, and availability of data-at-rest are protected

implementation_examples.title: Ex1
implementation_examples.text: Use encryption, digital signatures, and cryptographic hashes to protect the confidentiality and integrity of stored data in files, databases, virtual machine disk images, container images, and other resources

implementation_examples.title: Ex2
implementation_examples.text: Use full disk encryption to protect data stored on user endpoints

implementation_examples.title: Ex3
implementation_examples.text: Confirm the integrity of software by validating signatures

implementation_examples.title: Ex4
implementation_examples.text: Restrict the use of removable media to prevent data exfiltration

implementation_examples.title: Ex5
implementation_examples.text: Physically secure removable media containing unencrypted sensitive information, such as within locked offices or file cabinets

subcategories.category_text: Data are managed consistent with the organization's risk strategy to protect the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of information
subcategories.text: The confidentiality, integrity, and availability of data-in-transit are protected

implementation_examples.title: Ex1
implementation_examples.text: Use encryption, digital signatures, and cryptographic hashes to protect the confidentiality and integrity of network communications

implementation_examples.title: Ex2
implementation_examples.text: Automatically encrypt or block outbound emails and other communications that contain sensitive data, depending on the data classification

implementation_examples.title: Ex3
implementation_examples.text: Block access to personal email, file sharing, file storage services, and other personal communications applications and services from organizational systems and networks

implementation_examples.title: Ex4
implementation_examples.text: Prevent reuse of sensitive data from production environments (e.g., customer records) in development, testing, and other non-production environments

subcategories.category_text: Data are managed consistent with the organization's risk strategy to protect the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of information
subcategories.text: The confidentiality, integrity, and availability of data-in-use are protected

implementation_examples.title: Ex1
implementation_examples.text: Remove data that must remain confidential (e.g., from processors and memory) as soon as it is no longer needed

implementation_examples.title: Ex2
implementation_examples.text: Protect data in use from access by other users and processes of the same platform

subcategories.category_text: Data are managed consistent with the organization's risk strategy to protect the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of information
subcategories.text: Backups of data are created, protected, maintained, and tested

implementation_examples.title: Ex1
implementation_examples.text: Continuously back up critical data in near-real-time, and back up other data frequently at agreed-upon schedules

implementation_examples.title: Ex2
implementation_examples.text: Test backups and restores for all types of data sources at least annually

implementation_examples.title: Ex3
implementation_examples.text: Securely store some backups offline and offsite so that an incident or disaster will not damage them

implementation_examples.title: Ex4
implementation_examples.text: Enforce geographic separation and geolocation restrictions for data backup storage

subcategories.category_text: The hardware, software (e.g., firmware, operating systems, applications), and services of physical and virtual platforms are managed consistent with the organization's risk strategy to protect their confidentiality, integrity, and availability
subcategories.text: Configuration management practices are established and applied

implementation_examples.title: Ex1
implementation_examples.text: Establish, test, deploy, and maintain hardened baselines that enforce the organization's cybersecurity policies and provide only essential capabilities (i.e., principle of least functionality)

implementation_examples.title: Ex2
implementation_examples.text: Review all default configuration settings that may potentially impact cybersecurity when installing or upgrading software

implementation_examples.title: Ex3
implementation_examples.text: Monitor implemented software for deviations from approved baselines

subcategories.category_text: The hardware, software (e.g., firmware, operating systems, applications), and services of physical and virtual platforms are managed consistent with the organization's risk strategy to protect their confidentiality, integrity, and availability
subcategories.text: Software is maintained, replaced, and removed commensurate with risk

implementation_examples.title: Ex1
implementation_examples.text: Perform routine and emergency patching within the timeframes specified in the vulnerability management plan

implementation_examples.title: Ex2
implementation_examples.text: Update container images, and deploy new container instances to replace rather than update existing instances

implementation_examples.title: Ex3
implementation_examples.text: Replace end-of-life software and service versions with supported, maintained versions

implementation_examples.title: Ex4
implementation_examples.text: Uninstall and remove unauthorized software and services that pose undue risks

implementation_examples.title: Ex5
implementation_examples.text: Uninstall and remove any unnecessary software components (e.g., operating system utilities) that attackers might misuse

implementation_examples.title: Ex6
implementation_examples.text: Define and implement plans for software and service end-of-life maintenance support and obsolescence

subcategories.category_text: The hardware, software (e.g., firmware, operating systems, applications), and services of physical and virtual platforms are managed consistent with the organization's risk strategy to protect their confidentiality, integrity, and availability
subcategories.text: Hardware is maintained, replaced, and removed commensurate with risk

implementation_examples.title: Ex1
implementation_examples.text: Replace hardware when it lacks needed security capabilities or when it cannot support software with needed security capabilities

implementation_examples.title: Ex2
implementation_examples.text: Define and implement plans for hardware end-of-life maintenance support and obsolescence

implementation_examples.title: Ex3
implementation_examples.text: Perform hardware disposal in a secure, responsible, and auditable manner

subcategories.category_text: The hardware, software (e.g., firmware, operating systems, applications), and services of physical and virtual platforms are managed consistent with the organization's risk strategy to protect their confidentiality, integrity, and availability
subcategories.text: Log records are generated and made available for continuous monitoring

implementation_examples.title: Ex1
implementation_examples.text: Configure all operating systems, applications, and services (including cloud-based services) to generate log records

implementation_examples.title: Ex2
implementation_examples.text: Configure log generators to securely share their logs with the organization's logging infrastructure systems and services

implementation_examples.title: Ex3
implementation_examples.text: Configure log generators to record the data needed by zero-trust architectures

subcategories.category_text: The hardware, software (e.g., firmware, operating systems, applications), and services of physical and virtual platforms are managed consistent with the organization's risk strategy to protect their confidentiality, integrity, and availability
subcategories.text: Installation and execution of unauthorized software are prevented

implementation_examples.title: Ex1
implementation_examples.text: When risk warrants it, restrict software execution to permitted products only or deny the execution of prohibited and unauthorized software

implementation_examples.title: Ex2
implementation_examples.text: Verify the source of new software and the software's integrity before installing it

implementation_examples.title: Ex3
implementation_examples.text: Configure platforms to use only approved DNS services that block access to known malicious domains

implementation_examples.title: Ex4
implementation_examples.text: Configure platforms to allow the installation of organization-approved software only

subcategories.category_text: The hardware, software (e.g., firmware, operating systems, applications), and services of physical and virtual platforms are managed consistent with the organization's risk strategy to protect their confidentiality, integrity, and availability
subcategories.text: Secure software development practices are integrated, and their performance is monitored throughout the software development life cycle

implementation_examples.title: Ex1
implementation_examples.text: Protect all components of organization-developed software from tampering and unauthorized access

implementation_examples.title: Ex2
implementation_examples.text: Secure all software produced by the organization, with minimal vulnerabilities in their releases

implementation_examples.title: Ex3
implementation_examples.text: Maintain the software used in production environments, and securely dispose of software once it is no longer needed

subcategories.category_text: Security architectures are managed with the organization's risk strategy to protect asset confidentiality, integrity, and availability, and organizational resilience
subcategories.text: Networks and environments are protected from unauthorized logical access and usage

implementation_examples.title: Ex1
implementation_examples.text: Logically segment organization networks and cloud-based platforms according to trust boundaries and platform types (e.g., IT, IoT, OT, mobile, guests), and permit required communications only between segments

implementation_examples.title: Ex2
implementation_examples.text: Logically segment organization networks from external networks, and permit only necessary communications to enter the organization's networks from the external networks

implementation_examples.title: Ex3
implementation_examples.text: Implement zero trust architectures to restrict network access to each resource to the minimum necessary

implementation_examples.title: Ex4
implementation_examples.text: Check the cyber health of endpoints before allowing them to access and use production resources

subcategories.category_text: Security architectures are managed with the organization's risk strategy to protect asset confidentiality, integrity, and availability, and organizational resilience
subcategories.text: The organization's technology assets are protected from environmental threats

implementation_examples.title: Ex1
implementation_examples.text: Protect organizational equipment from known environmental threats, such as flooding, fire, wind, and excessive heat and humidity

implementation_examples.title: Ex2
implementation_examples.text: Include protection from environmental threats and provisions for adequate operating infrastructure in requirements for service providers that operate systems on the organization's behalf

subcategories.category_text: Security architectures are managed with the organization's risk strategy to protect asset confidentiality, integrity, and availability, and organizational resilience
subcategories.text: Mechanisms are implemented to achieve resilience requirements in normal and adverse situations

implementation_examples.title: Ex1
implementation_examples.text: Avoid single points of failure in systems and infrastructure

implementation_examples.title: Ex2
implementation_examples.text: Use load balancing to increase capacity and improve reliability

implementation_examples.title: Ex3
implementation_examples.text: Use high-availability components like redundant storage and power supplies to improve system reliability

subcategories.category_text: Security architectures are managed with the organization's risk strategy to protect asset confidentiality, integrity, and availability, and organizational resilience
subcategories.text: Adequate resource capacity to ensure availability is maintained

implementation_examples.title: Ex1
implementation_examples.text: Monitor usage of storage, power, compute, network bandwidth, and other resources

implementation_examples.title: Ex2
implementation_examples.text: Forecast future needs, and scale resources accordingly

subcategories.category_text: Assets are monitored to find anomalies, indicators of compromise, and other potentially adverse events
subcategories.text: Networks and network services are monitored to find potentially adverse events

implementation_examples.title: Ex1
implementation_examples.text: Monitor DNS, BGP, and other network services for adverse events

implementation_examples.title: Ex2
implementation_examples.text: Monitor wired and wireless networks for connections from unauthorized endpoints

implementation_examples.title: Ex3
implementation_examples.text: Monitor facilities for unauthorized or rogue wireless networks

implementation_examples.title: Ex4
implementation_examples.text: Compare actual network flows against baselines to detect deviations

implementation_examples.title: Ex5
implementation_examples.text: Monitor network communications to identify changes in security postures for zero trust purposes

subcategories.category_text: Assets are monitored to find anomalies, indicators of compromise, and other potentially adverse events
subcategories.text: The physical environment is monitored to find potentially adverse events

implementation_examples.title: Ex1
implementation_examples.text: Monitor logs from physical access control systems (e.g., badge readers) to find unusual access patterns (e.g., deviations from the norm) and failed access attempts

implementation_examples.title: Ex2
implementation_examples.text: Review and monitor physical access records (e.g., from visitor registration, sign-in sheets)

implementation_examples.title: Ex3
implementation_examples.text: Monitor physical access controls (e.g., locks, latches, hinge pins, alarms) for signs of tampering

implementation_examples.title: Ex4
implementation_examples.text: Monitor the physical environment using alarm systems, cameras, and security guards

subcategories.category_text: Assets are monitored to find anomalies, indicators of compromise, and other potentially adverse events
subcategories.text: Personnel activity and technology usage are monitored to find potentially adverse events

implementation_examples.title: Ex1
implementation_examples.text: Use behavior analytics software to detect anomalous user activity to mitigate insider threats

implementation_examples.title: Ex2
implementation_examples.text: Monitor logs from logical access control systems to find unusual access patterns and failed access attempts

implementation_examples.title: Ex3
implementation_examples.text: Continuously monitor deception technology, including user accounts, for any usage

subcategories.category_text: Assets are monitored to find anomalies, indicators of compromise, and other potentially adverse events
subcategories.text: External service provider activities and services are monitored to find potentially adverse events

implementation_examples.title: Ex1
implementation_examples.text: Monitor remote and onsite administration and maintenance activities that external providers perform on organizational systems

implementation_examples.title: Ex2
implementation_examples.text: Monitor activity from cloud-based services, internet service providers, and other service providers for deviations from expected behavior

subcategories.category_text: Assets are monitored to find anomalies, indicators of compromise, and other potentially adverse events
subcategories.text: Computing hardware and software, runtime environments, and their data are monitored to find potentially adverse events

implementation_examples.title: Ex1
implementation_examples.text: Monitor email, web, file sharing, collaboration services, and other common attack vectors to detect malware, phishing, data leaks and exfiltration, and other adverse events

implementation_examples.title: Ex2
implementation_examples.text: Monitor authentication attempts to identify attacks against credentials and unauthorized credential reuse

implementation_examples.title: Ex3
implementation_examples.text: Monitor software configurations for deviations from security baselines

implementation_examples.title: Ex4
implementation_examples.text: Monitor hardware and software for signs of tampering

implementation_examples.title: Ex5
implementation_examples.text: Use technologies with a presence on endpoints to detect cyber health issues (e.g., missing patches, malware infections, unauthorized software), and redirect the endpoints to a remediation environment before access is authorized

subcategories.text: Potentially adverse events are analyzed to better understand associated activities

implementation_examples.title: Ex1
implementation_examples.text: Use security information and event management (SIEM) or other tools to continuously monitor log events for known malicious and suspicious activity

implementation_examples.title: Ex2
implementation_examples.text: Utilize up-to-date cyber threat intelligence in log analysis tools to improve detection accuracy and characterize threat actors, their methods, and indicators of compromise

implementation_examples.title: Ex3
implementation_examples.text: Regularly conduct manual reviews of log events for technologies that cannot be sufficiently monitored through automation

implementation_examples.title: Ex4
implementation_examples.text: Use log analysis tools to generate reports on their findings

subcategories.text: Information is correlated from multiple sources

implementation_examples.title: Ex1
implementation_examples.text: Constantly transfer log data generated by other sources to a relatively small number of log servers

implementation_examples.title: Ex2
implementation_examples.text: Use event correlation technology (e.g., SIEM) to collect information captured by multiple sources

implementation_examples.title: Ex3
implementation_examples.text: Utilize cyber threat intelligence to help correlate events among log sources

subcategories.text: The estimated impact and scope of adverse events are understood

implementation_examples.title: Ex1
implementation_examples.text: Use SIEMs or other tools to estimate impact and scope, and review and refine the estimates

implementation_examples.title: Ex2
implementation_examples.text: A person creates their own estimates of impact and scope

subcategories.text: Information on adverse events is provided to authorized staff and tools

implementation_examples.title: Ex1
implementation_examples.text: Use cybersecurity software to generate alerts and provide them to the security operations center (SOC), incident responders, and incident response tools

implementation_examples.title: Ex2
implementation_examples.text: Incident responders and other authorized personnel can access log analysis findings at all times

implementation_examples.title: Ex3
